ES-01-354: From the plaza in Hondarribia at night, the glowing castle of Charles V rises above the old town walls. Its lit bulk dominates the walled quarter, warm light spilling from its windows onto the dark stone below. The narrow streets of the old town climb toward it, quiet under the castle's watch.
ES-01-355: From the harbor at Getaria at night, the town climbs its headland above a moonlit bay, the lighthouse beam sweeping steadily. Moonlight silvers the water while the fishing port's lights twinkle along the quay. The old town rises dark and compact on its promontory, the beam of the lighthouse pacing the night.
ES-01-356: From the mainland path at night, the islet of Gaztelugatxe rises from the dark sea, its little hermitage moonlit atop the rock. The stone footbridge arches across the water to it, pale in the moonlight. Waves move black below the bridge; the hermitage sits tiny and luminous on its pinnacle under the stars.
ES-01-357: From the old town square at night, Vitoria's cathedral presents its illuminated portico, the Gothic front glowing against the dark. Lit streets run away on either side, their lamps leading into the medieval quarter. The cathedral's tower rises behind the portico, the old town quiet around its lit heart.
ES-01-358: From the moat path at night, Ceuta's Royal Walls rise moonlit above the dark water of the moat. The massive fortifications catch the moon's light along their bastions while the water below lies black and still. The walls guard the narrow isthmus in silence, moonlight tracing their ancient stone.
ES-01-359: From the port at night, Melilla la Vieja's fortress rises above the harbor, its bastions floodlit and the lighthouse beam sweeping overhead. The illuminated ramparts glow against the dark Mediterranean while the modern port twinkles below. The old fortress commands the headland, light and stone holding the African shore.
ES-01-360: From the old town square at night, Logroño's Concatedral de Santa María de la Redonda rises with its twin towers floodlit against the sky. Lit streets of the old quarter run off the square, their tapas bars glowing. The twin towers dominate the night, the Rioja capital's old town humming softly below.
ES-01-361: From the plaza at night, the Puerta de Alcalá stands floodlit — its great neoclassical arches glowing against the black sky. The monument's stonework is warm under the lights, traffic circling the roundabout around it. Madrid's grandest gate keeps its lonely, luminous vigil at the edge of the Retiro.
ES-01-362: From the plaza at night, the University of Alcalá's plateresque façade glows under the floodlights, its carved front brilliant against the dark. The cloister beyond lies in softer light, the old college quiet after centuries of scholars. The illuminated façade is a monument to learning, radiant in the night.
ES-01-363: From the valley viewpoint at night, Albarracín's old town climbs its ridge in moonlight, the medieval walls tracing the hilltop. The pink-hued houses lie dark and quiet, alleys hidden in shadow, while the walls catch the moon's silver. Below, the Guadalaviar valley sleeps; above, the walled town keeps its ancient silhouette.
ES-01-364: From the hillside viewpoint at night, the Jerte valley falls away in moonlight, its gorge cutting dark between the slopes. The cherry orchards lie black and silent on the hillsides, a few scattered village lights below. Moonlight lays a pale wash over the valley, the night deep and still.
ES-01-365: From the cobbled street at night, Teruel's Torre de San Martín rises floodlit, its Mudejar brickwork glowing against the dark sky. The glazed tiles and patterned brick shine under the lights while the old town sleeps in shadow around it. The tower stands as the quarter's luminous beacon, centuries of Mudejar craft lit for the night.
ES-01-055: You stand on Calle Laurel in Logroño's old town, the famous tavern street, its bars' lights and signs glowing along the narrow lane. Shutters and balconies rise on both sides, with the street disappearing into shadow at either end. By day this lane is the capital of Rioja tapas; at night it holds its breath.
ES-01-056: Clavijo Castle stands on its crag against the night sky, the ruined walls caught by floodlight. Rock falls away on all sides while the dark Rioja valley spreads below. The site of the legendary battle of 844, still brooding over the land.
ES-01-057: Haro's old quarter sits above its famous vineyards, the town's lights spread below the dark hills. Church towers rise through the rooftops while the surrounding wine country is a black, rolling expanse. The wine capital of La Rioja, quiet before the next vintage.
ES-01-058: The cathedral of Santo Domingo de la Calzada rises over the old town, its tower and spire lit against the night. Pilgrim-route streets run below, shuttered and still, with the dark countryside beyond the rooftops. A thousand years of pilgrims have passed this way.
ES-01-059: The hilltop village of Briones stands over the Ebro valley, its stone houses and church silhouetted above the plain. Lights cluster along the ridge while the great dark valley stretches away beneath. One of Rioja's most beautifully placed villages, seen from its best side.
ES-01-060: Ezcaray's arcaded main street runs toward the church, the stone arches of the porticoes lining the darkened lane. A few lamps light the cobbles while the church front closes the view at the street's end. A mountain town of fine old houses, at rest.
ES-01-061: The abbey of Cañas rests in its valley, the monastery church and cloister caught by night lighting against the hills. The buildings sit quiet among dark fields with the ridgeline closing the background. A Cistercian house of rare elegance, founded in the twelfth century.
ES-01-062: Vine rows run over the dark hills of Rioja Alta, the trellised lines visible by starlight and distant farm lights. The rows climb and dip across the frame with the hills folding behind them. At this hour the vineyard is a vast, breathing geometry.
ES-01-063: The medieval pilgrim bridge of Puente la Reina crosses its river in a single elegant arc of stone. The arches stand out against the dark water, with the town's lights beyond and the banks lost in shadow. For centuries every pilgrim to Santiago has crossed here.
ES-01-064: The fortress walls and glacis of Pamplona's citadel run in long star-shaped lines through the night. Floodlit bastions catch the corners of the ramparts while the open glacis stretches empty and dark. The city's great military monument, silent at four in the morning.
ES-01-065: Javier Castle, the fortress-palace of Saint Francis Xavier, stands solid against the night sky. Its towers and crenellations are picked out by lighting while the surrounding Navarrese hills lie dark. The birthplace of the great missionary, still commanding its valley.
ES-01-066: Ochagavía's stone houses cluster in their Pyrenean valley, windows warm against the black slopes. The church rises among the roofs while the mountains close in on every side. A classic Pyrenean village, deep in the night of the Irati country.
ES-01-067: The gorge walls of the Foz de Lumbier rise sheer on both sides, rock faces barely visible in the dark. The river runs unseen far below while the cleft of sky overhead shows the stars. By day this is vulture country; at night it is all shadow and echo.
ES-01-068: The sanctuary-village of Ujué crowns its hill above the plains, the fortress-church lit at the summit. The plains spread dark and endless below while the village tumbles down the slopes. A watchtower of a town, guarding the lowlands from on high.
ES-01-069: Estella's old town rises above the river Ega, its Romanesque churches and old streets lit in the dark. The river glints faintly below while the rooftops climb the hillside. The Toledo of the north on the pilgrim road, at its most romantic.
ES-01-070: Viana's walled town stands over its vineyards, the old walls and church tower lit above the dark vines. The town fills the hilltop while the Rioja plain stretches black beyond. The last Navarrese town on the French Way, holding its hill through the night.
ES-01-071: From a forest track the great beech forest of Irati closes in on every side, trunks fading into darkness. The path runs between the trees with the canopy a black ceiling overhead. Europe's second-largest beech forest, ancient and utterly quiet.
ES-01-072: The great mouth of the Zugarramurdi caves opens from the hillside, the cavern's maw dark against the meadow. The stream runs out into the night while the surrounding grass lies still under the stars. The famous witches' cave, more mystery than menace at this hour.
ES-01-073: Lekeitio's harbour and basilica face the night sea, the great church rising above the port. Harbour lights reflect on the water while fishing boats lie dark at their moorings. A proud Basque fishing town, sleeping by the Cantabrian.
ES-01-074: At Itzurun beach the flysch strata of Zumaia rise in thin tilted layers, the rock sheets catching faint light. The beach lies dark at their feet while the sea is only sound beyond. These cliffs are a world-famous geological book, its pages lit by the moon.
ES-01-075: Zarautz's long beach curves below its old town, the promenade lights tracing the shoreline. The town rises behind the front with the dark hills at its back, and the sea lies flat and black beyond the sand. The Basque coast's grandest beach, empty at night.
ES-01-076: From the plaza you look up at Vitoria-Gasteiz's old town hill, the medieval streets and cathedral rising above. Lit windows climb the slope while the plaza lies quiet at your feet. The Basque capital's ancient core, a hill of history after midnight.
ES-01-077: Labastida's walled town sits among its vineyards, the old walls and church outlined above the dark vines. Town lights cluster within the walls while the Rioja Alavesa spreads black beneath. A wine town with its medieval bones still showing.
ES-01-078: Mundaka's estuary and port lie under the night sky, the harbour front lit along the water. The estuary mouth opens toward the sea while the town climbs behind the quay. Famous for its left-breaking wave; at night the water rests.
ES-01-079: The harbour town of Luarca folds around its cove, the white houses climbing the hillsides on both arms of the bay. Harbour lights shimmer on the water while the cemetery-topped headland stands dark. Asturias' prettiest port, a crescent of light in the dark.
ES-01-080: Lastres climbs its hillside above its port, the white houses stepped up the slope in the lamplight. The little harbour sits dark below while the Cantabrian Sea stretches black beyond. A fishing town stacked like an amphitheatre over the water.
ES-01-081: Tazones nestles in its cove, the little harbour village lit along the water's edge. Cliffs close the cove on either side while the sea lies dark beyond the harbour mouth. The port where Charles V first landed in Spain, dreaming in the dark.
ES-01-082: The braña pastures of Somiedo lie under the peaks, the high meadows dark between the mountain walls. A few shepherds' huts show faintly while the summits are black against the stars. The heart of the Cantabrian bear country, wild and silent.
ES-01-083: The famous bridge of Cangas de Onís arches over the Sella, its single great span and the hanging Victory Cross caught by the lighting. The river runs dark beneath while the banks are lost in shadow. The emblem of Asturias, and of the old kingdom's birth.
ES-01-094: The Tower of Hercules stands on its headland above the sea, the Roman lighthouse floodlit against the night. Waves break white on the rocks below while the city lights of A Coruña glow along the coast. The oldest working lighthouse in the world, still doing its job.
ES-01-095: The Obradoiro façade of Santiago cathedral fills the square, the baroque front floodlit in the small hours. The twin towers rise on either side while the empty plaza stretches at your feet. The goal of a thousand years of pilgrims, radiant in the dark.
ES-01-096: Ribadavia's old wine town lies along the river, its medieval streets and old quarter lit in warm patches. The castle ruins stand dark above the rooftops while the Miño valley sleeps beyond. Once the capital of the Ribeiro wine trade, still keeping its old stones.
ES-01-097: At Cambados the old tower stands at the water's edge, rising from the ría. The historic center's manor houses line the shore behind it while the water lies still and black. The heart of Albariño country, quiet by the tide.
ES-01-098: The hórreos of Combarro stand in their long row by the estuary, the stone granaries silhouetted against the water. A few lights burn in the old fishermen's quarter while the ría stretches dark beyond. Galicia's most photographed granaries, at their most atmospheric.
ES-01-099: The lighthouse of Cape Fisterra stands at the land's end, its beam sweeping the black Atlantic. Cliffs fall away on both sides while the rocks below catch the spray. The Romans called it the end of the world; at night you can believe it.
ES-01-100: From the lookout the red-earth mine of Las Médulas shows faintly under the night sky, the ruined pinnacles of the Roman workings. The jagged orange cliffs fill the frame with the chestnut forests dark below. The largest open-cast gold mine of the Roman Empire, still otherworldly.
ES-01-101: The stone village of Peñalba sits in the Aquilanos mountains, its slate roofs dark beneath the peaks. The little Mozarabic church stands among the houses, lit softly, while the mountains close the valley. One of Spain's most perfectly preserved mountain villages.
ES-01-102: Astorga's old town rises with its cathedral and Gaudí's Episcopal Palace standing close together, both lit against the night. The palace's fairy-tale turrets face the cathedral's bulk while the town spreads dark below. Two masterpieces, side by side in the small hours.
ES-01-103: León's Gothic cathedral stands with its two towers against the night sky, the great west front floodlit. The pinnacles and flying buttresses are etched in light while the square lies empty before it. The house of light keeps its stained glass sleeping until dawn.
ES-01-104: Burgos cathedral's twin spires rise over the city, the great Gothic mass floodlit in the dark. The lacework of the spires catches the light while the old town climbs the hill behind. Spain's third great Gothic cathedral, holding court over the night.
ES-01-105: Salamanca's Plaza Mayor glows in the small hours, the baroque arcades lit in their warm golden stone. The three closed sides of the square stand in perfect symmetry while the empty plaza floor stretches between them. Spain's most beautiful square, entirely yours at this hour.
ES-01-106: Zamora's cathedral rises with its famous scaled dome, the Byzantine-style cupola catching the night lighting. The Romanesque bulk of the church fills the frame while the old city lies dark around it. A dome like a stone pinecone, guarding the Duero.
ES-01-107: The Mendoza fortress at Manzanares el Real stands four-square against the night, its towers and the gallery of the upper court lit. The castle fills the frame above the town while the Pedriza mountains loom dark behind. One of Castile's finest fifteenth-century castles.
ES-01-108: The monastery of El Escorial rises in its vast grid, the basilica dome and twin towers floodlit against the sierra. The long granite facades run into the dark on either side while the courtyard lies silent. Philip II's great monument, severe and magnificent at night.
ES-01-109: Buitrago del Lozoya's medieval walls run in their river loop, the crenellated circuit lit along the water. The walls close the town on its peninsula while the river bends dark around them. A walled town in a river's embrace, almost an island.
ES-01-110: The Roman aqueduct of Segovia marches across the night in its double tier of granite arches. The great arcade is floodlit pier by pier while the old town rises behind it. Two thousand years old, holding up the sky without a drop of mortar.
ES-01-111: The monastery of El Paular rests in its mountain valley, the church and cloister lit among the dark pines. The valley walls rise on either side while the river runs unseen below. The first Carthusian house in Castile, deep in the Guadarrama night.
ES-01-112: From a second vantage the walls of Buitrago trace their river loop, the medieval circuit standing dark above the water. The town's lights cluster within the walls while the river bends black around the peninsula. A different angle on the walled town the Lozoya defends.
ES-01-113: Almudena Cathedral faces the Royal Palace across the square, both great masses floodlit in the night. The cathedral's dome and towers rise on one side while the palace's long facade runs on the other. Madrid's two giants, keeping watch over the sleeping city.
ES-01-114: The garden square of the Plaza de Oriente lies between palace and theatre, its clipped hedges and statues lit along the paths. The Royal Palace looms at one end while the opera house faces it from the other. Madrid's most stately square, at its quietest hour.
ES-01-127: You stand in the old plaza beneath the castle of Aínsa as the small hours settle over the Pyrenees foothills. Stone houses with shuttered windows line the square, the castle walls rising dark above them, with only streetlamps and a few lit windows breaking the night. A hushed, timeless view of one of Aragón's finest medieval towns.
ES-01-128: From outside the walls you take in the great star-shaped citadel of Jaca, its fortress ramparts standing with the Pyrenees looming behind. Floodlit bastions stand out against the black sky while the mountains are only a darker silhouette on the horizon. At four in the morning the whole place belongs to silence.
ES-01-129: Looking up at Tarazona's old town with the Moncayo massif filling the sky behind it. Lit balconies and the towers of the Mudéjar churches rise through the rooftops, and the great dark bulk of the mountain closes the frame. A quiet night view of a town where three cultures left their mark.
ES-01-130: The village of Alquézar clings to its crag above the Vero canyon, its few lights scattered across the dark rock. From below you see the lit windows of the stone houses and the collegiate church on its summit, the canyon a black void beneath. Night turns this eagle's-nest village into something out of a legend.
ES-01-131: In the park at Monasterio de Piedra the waterfalls run white against the black rock, caught by the park's lighting. Paths and spray fill the frame around the cascade, with ferns and cliff faces visible at the edges. The roar of falling water is the only company at this hour.
ES-01-132: Calatayud's old town spreads beneath its twin castle-crowned hills, with the Mudéjar towers of the churches standing out in the night. Lit streets trace the town grid below while the castle ruins sit dark against the sky. A handsome panorama of Aragón's city of the four towers.
ES-01-161: From the far shore of the harbour you look back across the still water toward Mahón, its lights doubled in the reflection. The town climbs the far hillside with church towers rising through the rooftops, and a few moored boats sit dark in the foreground. One of the Mediterranean's finest natural harbours, at its most peaceful.
ES-01-162: Night over Banyalbufar's terraced coast, where the stone-walled terraces step down toward the sea in darkness. Scattered lights from the village sit among the terraces while the Mediterranean lies flat and black beyond. You feel the whole slope breathing quietly under the stars.
ES-01-163: The walled old town of Alcúdia lies against the dark bay, its medieval ramparts faintly lit above the town. Windows glow within the walls while the water beyond shows only the faintest horizon line. A calm night portrait of Mallorca's Roman and medieval stronghold.
ES-01-164: Along the famous balcony-lined street of Santa Cruz de La Palma, the carved wooden balconies of the old houses stand out under the streetlamps. Doors and shutters are shut for the night, with only a few warm windows lit along the row. A quietly elegant street, asleep in the Canarian dark.
ES-01-165: Night in Teguise, the first capital of the Canary Islands, its whitewashed old town folded into the volcanic hills. Churches and old merchant houses show their outlines by lamplight, with the dark bulk of the volcanoes beyond. History hangs heavy here after midnight.
ES-01-166: The historic port town of San Sebastián lies quiet at night, its old streets and harbour front lit in warm pools. The tower of the church rises above the rooftops while the harbour water sits still and black. This is where Columbus last set foot in Europe before the Atlantic crossing.
ES-01-167: Under the stars the great dune field of Corralejo rolls toward the sea in pale moonlit waves. The sand crests catch what light there is while the Atlantic lies dark at the frame's edge. A desert by the ocean, vast and empty in the small hours.
ES-01-168: La Orotava's historic center climbs its hillside with the peak of Teide filling the sky behind it. Lit facades and the church towers stand out while the volcano is a great dark cone against the stars. The island's grandest old town, watched over by its giant.
ES-01-169: In Anaga the forest ridges and cliffs are pure night shapes, laurel forest cloaking the slopes with the ridgeline jagged against the sky. Only the faintest light from a distant village shows in the folds of the mountains. One of Europe's oldest and most atmospheric wild places.
ES-01-170: From Sacromonte the cave-quarter streets look across the ravine toward the Alhambra, its palaces floodlit gold on the hill opposite. Whitewashed cave houses glow softly at your feet while the fortress fills the center of the view. Night, flamenco silence, and the most famous view in Spain.
ES-01-115: You stand on the Golden Age square of Villanueva de los Infantes in the deep night, floodlights washing the old stone façades in a warm glow. The Plaza Mayor fills the frame, its arcades and lanterns standing out against the dark La Mancha sky. Windows flicker with a few late lights while the empty square holds the hush of 4 a.m., a Golden Age stage after the audience has gone home.
ES-01-116: From the edge of Pastrana's ducal old town at night, you look across a dark stone plaza toward the palace walls and church tower rising above the rooftops. The frame centers on the old town's historic profile, lit here and there by streetlamps that pick out carved stonework and quiet balconies. The whole scene is still, the way a ducal capital rests long after midnight.
ES-01-117: You face Almagro's arcaded Plaza Mayor at night, the long colonnade glowing under warm lamplight. Wooden galleries and stone columns run across the frame left to right, their shadows falling across the empty cobbles. The square is silent now, but the lit arcades keep the unmistakable shape of La Mancha's most theatrical town.
ES-01-118: From the plain below, you look up at Belmonte Castle standing floodlit against the night sky. The great fortress walls and towers fill the center of the frame, its floodlit stone cutting a bold silhouette while the dark countryside stretches out around it. After midnight the castle has the plain entirely to itself.
ES-01-119: At night the Lagunas de Ruidera lie dark and glassy, the lagoon chain stretching away under a star-flecked sky. Your viewpoint on the shore frames the water's still surface catching faint moonlight, with reeds and bank edges fading into darkness at either side. The night turns the famous waterfalls' chain into something quiet and mirror-like.
ES-01-120: Under the night sky, the Tablas de Daimiel wetlands spread out in a dark, shimmering expanse. Standing at the water's edge, you take in the lagoon surface with its reed beds and distant treeline just visible in the dim light. The frame holds the wetland's calm after dark — a rare quiet for one of Spain's most precious water landscapes.
ES-01-121: From the town below at night, the hilltop castle of Chinchilla de Montearagón glows above the rooftops. Floodlit walls and towers rise at the center of the frame over the dark slope, a commanding presence against the black sky. The old town sleeps at its foot while the castle keeps its ancient watch.
ES-01-122: You look up at Atienza's castle perched on its sheer rock outcrop in the night, floodlights tracing the fortress outline against the dark sky. The rock mass fills the frame's center, with the castle walls riding its summit and the town's dark rooftops clustering below. Few Spanish castles sit as dramatically as this one after dark.
ES-01-133: Standing on the Onyar riverfront at night, you take in Girona's famous painted houses glowing along the riverbank, with the cathedral's great mass rising behind them to the right. The lit façades reflect in the dark water, and the frame centers on the old town's postcard view at its most theatrical hour. After midnight the riverside is hushed, the city asleep behind its lights.
ES-01-134: At night in Tortosa, you face the old town across the dark Ebro, its streets and church towers lit in patches along the waterfront. The river fills the foreground of the frame, carrying reflected lamplight, while the old town climbs the far bank under the dark silhouette of La Suda castle hill. The night keeps the city's long history close and quiet.
ES-01-135: From the valley floor at night, Castellfollit de la Roca's houses line the edge of its great basalt cliff, their windows glowing warm against the black volcanic rock. The frame runs along the cliff-top village left to right, with the dark ravine dropping away beneath. Lit from within, the village looks like it's balanced on the very edge of the night.
ES-01-136: At night in Begur, you look up toward the old castle hill rising over the town, its walls dimly lit above the scattered house lights. The frame holds the medieval hill at the center with the Costa Brava coves lying dark somewhere beyond. The town glows softly below, a whitewashed cluster in the Empordà dark.
ES-01-137: In the volcanic country of La Garrotxa at night, Santa Pau's stone village glows warm among dark fields and volcanic hills. You stand at the village edge looking across its old walls and church tower, lit windows punctuating the frame. The night wraps the volcanic landscape in silence while the old streets keep their few lights.
ES-01-138: You stand on Vic's great arcaded main square at night, lamplight spilling from under the long rows of porches. The frame spans the Plaça Major's colonnades left and right, their arches glowing against the dark façades above. The cathedral square of the old episcopal city sits empty and calm in the early hours.
ES-01-139: From the town below at night, Cardona Castle crowns its hill in floodlit outline against the dark sky. The fortress walls and keep fill the center of the frame, raised above the dark salt-country rooftops. One of Catalonia's great castles, it keeps its proud profile through the night.
ES-01-140: At night, Siurana clings to its cliff-top in the dark, a scatter of warm window lights tracing the village silhouette. From your viewpoint below the crags, the frame centers on the lit houses edged by the black rock walls of the Montsant. The old frontier village holds the dark with its small stubborn lights.
ES-01-141: You stand on the Sitges waterfront at night, the church of Sant Bartomeu rising floodlit over the dark Mediterranean. The frame centers on the church against the sea, with the lit promenade curving away to either side. The night sea is black and calm, and the old town's lights make the shore glow.
ES-01-142: From the water at night, the walled island of Tabarca is a low ring of lights against the dark sea. You take in the whole island across the frame, its old walls and houses glowing softly with the lighthouse's pulse somewhere along the shore. The Mediterranean lies black all around, and the tiny island keeps its own quiet light.
ES-01-143: At night in Bocairent, you stand at the edge of the old Moorish quarter, its steep lanes and whitewashed houses lit in patches against the dark hillside. The frame climbs through the old quarter's rooftops toward the night sky. The quarter's maze of lanes sleeps, its few lit windows watching over the valley.
ES-01-144: From the sea at night, Altea's white town rises over the dark water with its famous blue-tiled dome glowing at the crown. You face the old town's profile across the frame, whitewashed houses climbing the hill under the floodlit church. The night Mediterranean laps the shore while the town shines against the dark.
ES-01-145: At night, Vilafamés glows on its hilltop, the village's stone houses and castle walls lit warm against the dark Maestrat. From the plain below you take in the whole hilltop settlement across the frame, rising from black fields into the night sky. The old artist's village keeps its hill like a lantern in the dark.
ES-01-146: Standing in the old town of Sant Mateu at night, you face its stone houses and old church towers under scattered lamplight. The frame holds the Maestrazgo town's historic center, Gothic palaces and quiet streets dimmed to warm pools of light. The night brings out the old capital's stern, handsome calm.
ES-01-147: From the port at night, Dénia Castle glows on its hill above the dark harbor. The frame centers on the floodlit fortress with the town lights spread below and the black sea to the right. Moorish walls keep their watch over the Costa Blanca through the early hours.
ES-01-148: At night, Cullera Castle stands floodlit on its ridge above the dark bay. You look up from the shore toward the lit walls at the frame's center, with the town's scattered lights below and the Mediterranean stretching black to the horizon. The castle holds the ridge like a beacon over the sleeping bay.
ES-01-149: From the town below at night, Sagunto Castle stretches along its hilltop in a long lit line against the dark sky. The frame runs with the ancient fortress walls left to right above the sleeping town. Two thousand years of stone keep their line through the night.
ES-01-150: You stand on the Villajoyosa seafront at night, the famous colored houses glowing in their bright façades along the dark beach. The frame runs along the waterfront's painted fronts — pinks, blues, and yellows under the lamplight — with the night sea to the right. The old fishing town wears its colors even after dark.
ES-01-151: From the shore at night, Águilas Castle crowns its headland in floodlit silhouette over the black Mediterranean. The frame centers on the lit fortress above the town's scattered lights, with dark water on both sides of the point. The old watch castle keeps its headland against the night sea.
ES-01-152: At night, Cehegín's old town glows on its hill, Baroque church towers lit above the clustered rooftops. From below you take in the hilltop across the frame, the town's lights rising out of the dark northwest Murcia countryside. The old town keeps its high seat through the quiet hours.
ES-01-153: Standing on the rocks of Cabo de Palos at night, you face the lighthouse sweeping its beam over the dark Mediterranean. The frame centers on the lit tower with black water all around and the faint far lights of La Manga to one side. The cape's light keeps its slow rhythm through the small hours.
ES-01-154: At night the Calblanque coves lie dark and undisturbed, black sand and clear water under a starlit sky. From the shore path you look across the frame's curve of cove beaches, the sea faintly silvered and the protected dunes just shapes in the dark. The wild coast sleeps with nobody on it.
ES-01-155: From the valley at night, Lorca Castle glows along its ridge above the dark town. The frame holds the long fortress line floodlit against the black sky, with Lorca's lights spread below in the Guadalentín valley. The Sun Fortress keeps its valley through the night.
ES-01-156: At night in Caravaca de la Cruz, the sanctuary castle glows on its hill over the sleeping town. From the streets below you look up at the floodlit fortress walls at the frame's center, the town's lights falling away downhill. The holy city keeps its vigil in the dark.
ES-01-157: From the air's vantage at night, La Manga is a thin strip of light strung between two black seas — the Mediterranean on one side, the Mar Menor on the other. The frame runs with the glowing ribbon of the strip, its hotels and streets lit against the dark water on both flanks. A narrow world of light between two night seas.
ES-01-158: At night in Jumilla, the castle hill rises floodlit over the dark wine country. You face the lit fortress across the frame with the sleeping vineyards stretching black around the town's scattered lights. The old wine capital keeps its hill lit through the small hours.
